hmm1.name: Latent-pathway / regulatory reversibility hypothesis
hmm1.hypothesis: Recent white states in young East Asian Cirsium may often reflect suppression of a retained anthocyanin/flavonoid programme rather than irreversible pathway destruction.
predictions: recent white lineages retain intact core structural genes
regulatory/expression changes recur more often than destructive coding loss
candidate coloured reversals restore retained machinery
deep independent white lineages may use more heterogeneous routes than within-lineage polymorphisms
hmm1.falsifier: replicated recent white lineages independently lose essential core pathway genes with no retained functional route

takaoense_six_morph_linked_samples.boundary: regain is topology-sensitive and not identified by the published figure alone

arenicola.boundary: ancestral colour is not identified without transition-rate constraints; published time information alone does not resolve loss-versus-regain polarity

aza3_use: Treat pathway reactivation as a mechanistic hypothesis only after an independent historical gate establishes an admissible loss->regain event or explicitly label the analysis as suppression-without-demonstrated-regain.
